thread.title: Earnings Season For The Dow Challenged By Negative Weekly Charts

author: Richard Henry Suttmeier
title: Earnings Season For The Dow Challenged By Negative Weekly Charts
text:
Stocks Above Their Five-Week Modified Moving Average McDonalds (MCD) ended last week above its five-week modified moving average of $160.08. MCD reports earnings on April 24.
Nike (NKE) ended last week above its five-week modified moving average of $66.22. NKE reported quarterly earnings for its earnings ended in February on March 22 and beat analysts’ estimates.
UnitedHealth (UNH) ended last week above its five-week modified moving average of $222.84. UNH will report quarterly earnings on April 17.
Stocks That Are Oversold
General Election (GE): Do not buy until GE gets booted from the Dow 30.
Home Depot (HD): Does not report earnings until May 15.
Merck (MRK): Reports earnings on May 1.
Procter & Gamble (PG): Reports earnings on April 20.
Verizon (VZ): Reports earnings on April 24.
Walmart (WMT) – Does not report earnings until May 17.
Exxon Mobil (XOM) – Reports earnings on April 27.
Among the Dow stocks only General Electric and Walmart are in bear market territory, 32.6% and 21.2% below their 2018 highs respectively. Eighteen stocks are in correction territory, down between 10% and 20% from their 2018 highs. Ten are down between 3.8% and 9.8% since their 2018 highs.
Nike is just 3.8% below its all-time intraday high of $70.25 set on Feb.27
Here’s A Dow 30 Scorecard
Global Marker Consultants The Dow 30
The Dow Jones Industrial Average is in correction territory, down 10.1% below its all-time intraday high of 26,616.71 set on Jan 26. The average is down 3.2% year-to-date.
Eight components set new year-to-date lows in April along with the Dow 30, which set its 2018 low of 23,344.52 on April 2: Caterpillar (CAT), Walt Disney (DIS), DowDuPont (DWDP), Home Depot (HD), 3M (MMM), Merck (MRK), Walmart (WMT) and ExxonMobil (XOM).
Only five stocks set their all-time intraday highs on March 13: Apple (AAPL), Cisco Systems (CSCO), Goldman Sachs (GS), Intel (INTC) and Microsoft (MSFT).
Twelve components are outperforming the Dow: Apple, Boeing (BA), Cisco, Goldman Sachs, IBM (IBM), JPMorgan Chase (JPM), Microsoft, Nike, Pfizer (PFE), Travelers (TRV), UnitedHealth Group (UNH) and Visa (V).
These statistics makes in impossible to recommend new long-term investments now as first quarter earnings season begins. JP Morgan (JPM) reports before the opening bell on Friday, April 13.
